metadata.note: Kokomo, Indiana had passenger trains for about 117 years, from 1854 to 1971, on three steam railroads. The first was the Peru and Indianapolis Railroad, which reached Kokomo in 1854 along Buckeye Street and made the town its terminus before pushing on to Peru and Michigan City; that line was the oldest trackage in what became the Nickel Plate system, joining the Lake Erie and Western in 1887 and the Nickel Plate in 1922. The Pennsylvania Railroad's route to Logansport opened on July 4 1855, celebrated locally under the name Cincinnati and Chicago Railroad. The third and, by contemporary accounts, the most important was the Clover Leaf, which began as the Frankfort and Kokomo Railroad of 1873-74 and gained its eastern connection at Kokomo on January 1 1881, growing into the Toledo, St. Louis and Kansas City and then the Toledo, St. Louis and Western before the Nickel Plate absorbed it too. Kokomo's Lake Erie and Western depot of 1916 survives and is on the National Register. Passenger service ended with the Pennsylvania Railroad depot going freight-only after April 30 1971 - the day before Amtrak began. A fourth passenger operator, the Indianapolis-Logansport/Peru interurban of the Indiana Union Traction Company and later the Indiana Railroad, ran through Kokomo from 1903 to 1938 but is not drawn here; see incomplete_coverage.

geometry_sources: OpenStreetMap railway ways (railway=rail/disused/abandoned/razed/dismantled) fetched by bounding box and assembled with a corridor-constrained shortest path: ways are kept only if they run within 6 km of a corridor through the documented towns, each graph edge is weighted by length times a penalty for straying from the corridor, ways tagged to a different historic operator are penalised eightfold, and straight connectors between fragments carry a flat sixfold penalty so they are used only where the mapped track genuinely does not join. No OSM route relation covers any of Kokomo's lines - the relations in the area (PRR Main Line Columbus-Chicago, NS Marion and Frankfort Districts, CSX Frankfort Secondary) all pass more than 20 km away.
metadata.incomplete_coverage: NOT DRAWN: (1) The Indianapolis-Logansport/Peru interurban, run by the Indiana Union Traction Company 1903-1930 and the Indiana Railroad 1930-1938, which reached Kokomo from Indianapolis via Carmel, Cicero, Arcadia, Atlanta, Tipton, Sharpsville and Fairfield. Its dates are well sourced - first southbound car through Carmel October 31 1903, regular Logansport-Kokomo schedule July 28 1904, Peru line opened August 14 1904, Logansport service discontinued September 15 1930, passenger service replaced by buses September 6 1938 - but OSM carries only a single way named 'Indiana Railroad Interurban' in the whole two-degree box, so there is nothing to trace. (2) The Lake Erie and Western south of Tipton to Indianapolis: 16 km of that corridor has no mapped track in OSM. (3) The Clover Leaf and Lake Erie and Western beyond Marion and Peru respectively, which are outside the Kokomo area this layer covers.
metadata.not_yet_sourced: The dates Kokomo's Nickel Plate lines actually lost their passenger trains. Both the Lake Erie and Western and the Clover Leaf features are drawn to 1965, the Nickel Plate's system-wide end of passenger service, because no source found gives a branch-specific discontinuance date; local service on these Indiana branches, which faced heavy interurban competition, very likely ended well before that, so 1965 should be read as an upper bound rather than a fact. One low-quality search result claimed Nickel Plate passenger service on the line ceased in 1932 under interurban competition, but that claim does not appear in the American-Rails history and is recorded here rather than adopted. Also unsourced: the corporate succession of the Kokomo-Logansport line between the Cincinnati and Chicago Railroad of 1855 and the Pennsylvania Railroad - the 1882 split used here is the year the PRR is documented to have taken running rights in the Kokomo area, not a documented change of ownership on this line; and all headways.

metadata.rule4_audit: 2026-08-27: prr-kokomo-logansport ran a single segment from 1882 to 1971 under the Pennsylvania Railroad's name and colour, quietly spanning the 1 February 1968 Penn Central merger. Split at 1968 into two features on identical geometry, the later one recoloured to Penn Central's #1A1A1A. Found while adding kokomo_connections.geojson, which draws the Logansport-Chicago line these trains connected to and which splits at the same date.
metadata.now_connected: 2026-08-27: the three corridors in this file are no longer isolated. kokomo_connections.geojson adds Indianapolis-Tipton and Peru-Michigan City (completing the Lake Erie and Western's Indianapolis Division), Marion-Toledo (the Clover Leaf's eastern end) and Logansport-Chicago (the Pennsylvania's Columbus-to-Chicago main line). The Clover Leaf west of Frankfort to East St. Louis is still missing; see that file's still_not_connected field.

segments.note: The first railroad into Kokomo. Incorporated January 19 1846, this was the oldest trackage in what became the Nickel Plate system; frequency estimated, unsourced
